newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon trade deficit $562 mln in July.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon trade deficit $562 mln in July.

text.p: Lebanon had a July trade deficit of $561.8 million compared with a June shortfall of $506.1 million, the Bank of Lebanon said in its latest monthly bulletin on Wednesday.
It brought the accumulated deficit for the first seven months of 1996 to $3.594 billion compared with $3.725 billion in the same period of 1995.
Year-to-date imports were $4.151 billion and exports were $556.6 million compared with $4.159 billion and $434.9 million last year, the Bank said.
This was a 0.1 percent fall in imports and a 28.9 percent increase in exports during the first seven months of the year.

July imports were $668 million, a rise of 15.1 percent over June and 4.5 percent higher than July 1995, the Bank said. July exports were $106.2 million -- 4.3 percent up on June, and 37.4 percent higher than July 1995.
Total customs receipts -- the biggest component of government revenue -- were 132.4 billion Lebanese pounds, an increase of 4.3 percent over June and a 13.9 percent rise over July 1995.
